text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Russian author BORIS PASTERNAK, famed for his prize-winning novel "DOCTOR ZHIVAGO", was born on this day in 1890.
American comedian JIMMY DURANTE, whose large nose became part of his very successful act, was born in 1893.
Actor RAY BOLGER, who played the "straw man" in the WIZARD OF OZ, was born in 1904.
American film and television actor ROBERT WAGNER, twice married to NATALIE WOOD, was born in 1930.

US singer and pianist ROBERTA FLACK was born in 1939. She was discovered in the late sixties and got a recording contract in 1969. Her solo hits include "The First Time I Ever Saw Your Face" (1972), "Killing Me Softly With His Song" (1973) and "Feel LIke Making Love"(1974). Hits with DONNY HATHAWAY included "Where Is The Love" (1972), "The Closer I Get To You" (1978) and "Back Together Again" (1980). Sucessful duets with PEABO BRYSON included "Tonight I Celebrate My Love" (1983).

Australian singer/songwriter and pianist PETER ALLEN was born in 1944. He was also briefly married to LIZA MINELLI. He wrote hits for fellow Australian OLIVIA NEWTON-JOHN such as "I Honestly Love You". He also had success singing his own compositions such as "I Go To Rio".
Champion Australian golfer GREG NORMAN, known as "The Great White Shark" and currently ranked number-one in the world, was born on this day in 1958.
**EVENTS**
1763: The TREATY OF PARIS was signed, ending 7-years of world-wide war.
1840: Britain's QUEEN VICTORIA married her first cousin PRINCE ALBERT.
1889: The use of the revised Bible was authorised by the Church of England.
1913 : Rescuers found the bodies of British polar explorer Captain ROBERT SCOTT and two companions, after they'd disappeared on an expedition to the South Pole.
1923: German physicist WILLIAM RONTGEN, who invented the x-ray, died.
1932: EDGAR WALLACE, the British novelist who wrote detective stories and film scripts, died.
1942: American bandleader GLENN MILLER was presented with a gold pressing of his hugely popular record "CHATTANOOGA CHOO CHOO". It was the first record ever to sell a million copies.

1955: Thousands of armed South African Police evicted 60,000 blacks from their homes in Sophiatown, near Johannesburg, as part of the Government's apartheid policy. Blacks later dubbed the 'South Western Townships' "SOWETO" - as "so where to ?".
1961: American author DASHIEL HAMMETT, who was hounded by the McCARTHY 'Un-American' trials of the 1950's, died.
1962: American spy-plane pilot GARY POWERS and top KGB spy Colonel RUDOLF ABEL were involved in an historic prisoner-exchange in Berlin.

1964: In Australia's worst peacetime naval disaster 82 lives were lost when the aircraft carrier HMAS MELBOURNE collided with the destroyer HMAS VOYAGER. The destroyer's forward section took just ten minutes to sink after the vessel was cut in half by the MELBOURNE. Both ships were blacked out for exercises about 20 miles off the Jervis Bay Naval Base in New South Wales. The VOYAGER turned across the path of the carrier and the captain R.J. ROBERTSON said he saw the two halves of the destroyer float past either side as he brough the MELBOURNE to a halt. VOYAGER's captain DUNCAN HERBERT STEVENS, aged 43, died on his ship. There were 242 survivors from the crew of 324. At least one Voyager disaster survivor has won a compensation case against the Federal Government.
1971: COCO CHANEL, who went from humble beginnings to become one of the giants of the fashion-world, died.
1973: Australia's first legal casino opened at Wrest Point in Tasmania.
1988: Octogenarian English actor Sir JOHN GIELGUD played the longest role for a man of his years. It was the part of SYDNEY COCKERELL in "The Best Of Friends" by HUGH WHITMORE.

1994: Australia's former federal sports minister ROS KELLY told a Parliamentary Inquiry that she used a whiteboard when working out sports grants for organisations around the country. The fact that she had no permanent record of the decision making process caused her to be the butt of numerous jibes from her parliamentary opponents and the subject of jokes for many. She resigned as Sports minister 18 days later as she came under increasing pressure from the opposition about what was called the "sports rorts". ROS KELLY resigned from politics in January 1995.
